habits.boundary_condition: The exact room count and bed mix should scale with the trip context; evidence includes two rooms/bedrooms for some group trips and three rooms for a larger group trip.
habits.condition: When booking a hotel for a family or small group where several people need sleeping space.
habits.default_action: Search for hotels offering at least two separate rooms or bedrooms, and confirm the bed setup in each room before treating an option as suitable.
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply to solo, couple-only, or otherwise small-party stays unless the user again requests separate rooms or specific beds.
habits.name: multi_room_sleeping_space_for_group_hotel_stays
habits.preference_value: For group or family hotel stays, the traveler tends to prefer multiple separate rooms/bedrooms with explicit bed arrangements, rather than a single standard room.
habits.rationale: Across three independent hotel dialogues, the user repeatedly avoids assuming a single room is enough and instead asks for multiple rooms or bedrooms plus sleeping-space/bed details.

source_evidence.contribution: Supports the multi-bedroom default for family travel and frames it as needed sleeping space rather than a generic hotel slot.
source_evidence.exact_user_quote: We have four children. I'm going to need a hotel that offers at least two bedrooms.

source_evidence.contribution: Independently supports a preference for multiple rooms with explicit bed configuration.
source_evidence.exact_user_quote: Looking for two rooms. One room needs to have two twin beds and the other room a queen-size bed.

source_evidence.contribution: Independently supports not defaulting to a single room for group hotel stays; the user asks for multiple rooms.
